key_insight: OPD generally trails GRPO in accuracy per training FLOP with external teachers, but efficiently consolidates domain-specific GRPO experts into one student.
engineering_relevance: Training domain specialists with GRPO and consolidating them via multi-teacher OPD can reduce total compute versus joint GRPO while preserving specialist-level accuracy.
method: Compare reverse-KL OPD and GRPO using held-out accuracy versus training FLOPs.
Vary task difficulty, model sizes, domain, optimization, and teacher source.
Distill domain-specific GRPO checkpoints into a single student using multi-teacher OPD.
evidence_signal: OPD recovered a GRPO checkpoint’s math accuracy with 50× fewer distillation FLOPs; multi-teacher distillation cost 5.2% and 8.0% of specialist training FLOPs for two and four domains, respectively, and the two-domain pipeline used 42.0% fewer total FLOPs than joint GRPO.
watch_item: The 50× result excludes teacher training: single-domain distillation adds compute to an already usable checkpoint, and external-teacher OPD often inflates response length.
paper_title: Unpacking the Compute Efficiency of Strong-to-Weak OPD against GRPO
